headline: At six levels the per-level mechanisms have doubled again while the css-prop fold has not moved a measurable amount, which is the clearest statement in the study of what compiling a chain is worth.

microbench.why: `vanilla` (0.503 ms/1k) and `next-yak-css-9.7` (0.517) are indistinguishable from their own depth-1 figures, the fold having concatenated six levels into one class on one element. Everything that merges at render pays six times: `bamboo` 1.13 ms/1k on six `cx()` joins, `stylex-layers` 1.36 through `styleq`, `tailwind-merge` 2.49 on six merges, `panda` 3.47 re-resolving six objects for 2.39 ms of component self-time. The 9.6.0 runtime at 5.07 ms/1k is six nested `Yak` components per instance, the steepest line in the case.

autocannon.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` 1,540 req/s, unchanged from depth 1, against `vanilla`'s 1,470. `panda` at 138 req/s is the floor and `tailwind-merge` at 345 pays six merge calls per element; the 9.6.0 runtime at 188 shows what six React components per instance cost under load.

attribution.why: `vanilla` (0.603 ms) and `next-yak-css-9.7` (0.630) are the react-dom floor. `panda` puts 2.39 of its 3.74 ms into component self-time, 63.7 ms of a 99.5 ms JS window inside its own package. `tailwind-merge` spends 1.99 ms of library time and 55.7 ms in its own package on six merges, `stylex-layers` 0.212 of library plus 0.361 of component through `styleq`, and the 9.6.0 runtime 4.93 ms of library. next-yak's styled API holds 0.971 ms, its perf runtime having collapsed the `Yak → Yak` chain to a single component.

hydrate.why: 48.4-67.0 ms of pure JS for the lanes with a finished sheet, no style or layout in the span. `styled-components` (104 ms) and `goober` (117) inject during hydration; `emotion` at 79.3 ms re-serializes six levels of rules on the client.

inp.why: One button's subtree re-renders and most lanes land at 6.5-8.6 ms, under 0.8 ms of span JS. Depth reaches the interaction only where something runs per level: `panda` needs 15.3 ms re-resolving six merged objects, and the 9.6.0 runtime 24.4 ms rendering six components for the element that changed.

mount.why: 72.7-97.2 ms for the lanes that mount a finished sheet. `emotion` and `goober` both reach 117 ms and `emotion`'s 15.7 ms layout against the cluster's 5.8-7.9 is the browser waiting on the injected sheet; the 9.6.0 runtime at 103 ms pays before first paint for a different reason, six components per element.

renderTiming.why: One recalculation, one layout, two paints; the counts tie across every lane. Six levels of composition change the class attribute's length, not how many times the browser recalculates a static sheet, and recalc cost stays inside 0.129-0.215 ms.

payload.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` still ships 2.66 kB gzipped at depth 6, the same figure as at depth 1, because six levels of declarations collapse into the same numbered classes. `vanilla` needs 3.08 kB by hand. `bamboo` (5.65 kB) and `panda` (9.07) carry six class tokens per element in the markup, and the difference between `panda` here and at depth 1 is almost entirely HTML, 3.16 to 3.98 kB.

nsweep.why: `vanilla` (2.07 ms at n=4,000) and `next-yak-css-9.7` (2.17) are flat. Depth multiplies into the sweep everywhere else: `bamboo` 4.63 ms, `stylex-layers` 5.44, `tailwind-merge` 9.93, and `panda` 20.8 alongside the 9.6.0 runtime's 20.7, both an order of magnitude above the fold on the same component tree.

crossCase: Reading the ladder against the Examples `compose-1` and `compose-3` shown above, `next-yak-css-9.7` costs 0.522, 0.517 and 0.517 ms/1k on 2.67, 2.66 and 2.66 kB, so composition is free to it in both time and bytes. Every per-level mechanism roughly doubles from depth 1 to depth 6: `bamboo` 0.553 to 1.13, `stylex-layers` 0.530 to 1.36, `tailwind-merge` 0.540 to 2.49, `panda` 1.18 to 3.47, and the 9.6.0 runtime 1.17 to 5.07. next-yak's styled API moves only 0.448 to 0.698 because its perf runtime flattens the chain, but it keeps a residual wrapper wherever a styled component wraps another component.
